events.text: Framed AMZN as an 'AI laggard→winner' transition, with the OpenAI deal adding ~$100B to backlog at the print and AI ARR >$15B / chips >$20B.

Called AWS 'my favorite business', with Jassy's redemption arc (OpenAI $50B + Anthropic = 'two AI winners solidified', Trainium3/4 sold out); ~$50B if Trainium were an external chip program vs Broadcom's ~$100B AI-semi target.

Preview math: ~$150B of the $200B FY26 capex is AWS-driven (~100% of AWS revenue), implying a build toward ~$400B of AWS revenue; lower AI-deal margins (~10-20%) and Q2 margin risk as Anthropic ramps.

Revenue $181.5B, +17% y/y; OI $23.9B; op margin 13.1% (record). AWS +28% y/y (fastest in 15 quarters), +$2B q/q, $150B run-rate. AWS backlog $364B (excludes the >$100B Anthropic deal). Custom silicon >$20B run-rate, +40% q/q; Trainium commitments >$225B. Q2'26 guide: sales $194-199B, OI $20-24B (helped by Prime Day moving into Q2).

Called the OI guide 'very conservative' and read the revenue guide as implying continued AWS acceleration to 'low-to-mid 30s'. ~$20B of the sequential step-up is non-frontier-lab, the largest ever recorded; Trainium 30-40% better price/perf allows it to 'save billions in capex and extract margin points'.

AWS grew 28% with better-than-expected 1Q margins and 'no one-timers' (mgmt reframed the historical range as effectively just 'low-30s'); Trainium saves AWS 'several hundred bps' of margin vs renting Nvidia GPUs; Bedrock model-access revenue is booked NET. AWS margins are low only because it is a 'newer-stage, more capital-intensive' business.
Cut AWS web-metric color, weakening for 4 weeks, 'Q4 risk' in non-AI cloud growth. Maintains Outperform, $315.
Flagged 'unusually flat' non-AI cloud SSO growth in May, with non-AI cloud 4Q growth at risk if it persists.

The June-26 Russell reclassification moves ~600bps of Amazon into the Russell 1000 Value benchmark (AMZN goes to ~zero in the 1000 Growth) — a mechanical flow event (forced selling of 'winners'), part of a Mag7 growth→value rotation.

Corroborates the AWS re-acceleration (+28%, $150bn run-rate, $364bn backlog excluding Anthropic >$100bn); >$225bn of Trainium revenue commitments from Anthropic+OpenAI. Funding: capex ~$200bn FY26 → ~$300bn FY27E → ~$350bn FY28E; TTM FCF collapsed to ~$1bn (from ~$26bn the year before). AMZN responded with ~$67bn of bonds in 1H + a $17.5bn term loan — ~$85bn of new funding capacity in <6 months without touching equity, read as pre-funding the FY27 ramp.

Amazon ad FY ~27% (sponsored products 65% of spend, softening to ~+16% May vs +21% April), but video ads +83% y/y and DSP +77% y/y, both accelerating; Amazon 'declared war' on The Trade Desk (take rate 20% vs 1%).

Hyperscaler bull case: the AWS/GCP accelerations are not explained by hourly accelerator rental alone — the hyperscalers are increasingly the distribution endpoint for the frontier labs (enterprises deploying Claude Code via AWS/Azure). Lower gross margin but powerful upsell; investor mood on AMZN/MSFT/ORCL 'more mixed than I would expect'.

BofA Buy, PO $310. MS (Nowak) flags the SpaceX compute deal at $50/watt as ~16% of upside to AWS '27 revenue if monetization reaches $25/watt. Prime Day (96 hrs, starting Jun-23) estimated by BofA at ~$22B of GMV (≈+5% y/y).

OW, Dec-26 PT $330 (~32x 2027E GAAP EPS $10.38), AMZN Best Idea / Analyst Focus List. Prime 'unbundled' worth ~$1,440/year vs the $139 cost (~10x); 370M+ global subs at year-end 2026 (~139M US / ~231M Int'l); ~$7B-$8B of Prime Day revenue shifted into Q2'26; a $20 hike in the US price ≈ ~$3B of annualized sales, now seen slipping from 2026 to 2027.

'The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC' — Overweight, PT $330 = ~25x an average of $13 of '27/'28 EPS (≈29x '27 / ≈22x '28), bull $400 (~27x an average of $15), bear $210 (~17x an average of $12); spot $232.11, mean consensus PT $309.55 (range $207-$370), 94% OW; options-implied P(>$330) ~11.3% vs P(<$210) ~39.7% — the bear case at nearly 4x the base, the most skewed of MS's four internet names and a hard counterweight to the 'consensus long / most crowded MAG7' positioning. The headline driver is the most aggressive AWS line on the page: AWS revenue growth 19.7% (2025) → 34.9% (26e) → 40.2% (27e) → 36.2% (28e), with the 40.2% above GS ~35%, JPM's FY26 +32.4% and the 35-36% buy-side bogey — MS models a further acceleration into 2027 rather than a plateau at the exit rate. MS vs cons FY Dec-26e: revenue 826,010 vs 823,989; EBITDA 223,360 vs 212,257; EPS 9.59 vs 8.82. The framework that matters most here is the third one: a model-enabled API run on 3P/RENTED infrastructure at $7.75/hr yields $40.5bn/GW of revenue less ~$28bn of compute cost = $12.6bn EBIT (~31% margin, ~25% NOPAT margin) — the first published attempt to split the token dollar between the model lab and the infrastructure owner, landing on the hyperscaler keeping roughly $28bn of the $40.5bn/GW pool. That is the quantified version of the Bedrock/TaaS front-end mechanic, and the owned-vs-rented spread (~46% ROIC owned vs ~25% NOPAT margin rented) is exactly where AWS's Trainium/Graviton vertical integration sits. MS: 'we remain bullish AWS, GCP and Azure,' with the caveat that reported near-term incremental margins run below the band.

AWS's TSMC CoWoS share slips but the wafers accelerate — read the denominator, not the percentage. Fubon's customer-mix forecast has AWS at 14.1% (2023) → 12.4% (2024) → 12.7% (2025) → 10.9% (2026) → 10.4% (2027), while the wafer counts behind those shares run 18,200 → 37,220 → 85,650 → 127,500 → 196,500, i.e. +49% in 2026 and +54% in 2027, on a total pool going 675,000 (2025) → 1,155,600 shipped / 1,170,000 capacity (2026) → 1,890,000 (2027). The pool grows +64% in 2027 while AWS grows +54%, so the declining share is a denominator effect, not an allocation cut. AWS remains the third-largest CoWoS customer behind NVDA (50.0% / 945,000 wafers) and AVGO (22.3% / 421,800), ahead of AMD (7.0% / 132,300) and MSFT (1.0% / 18,900, entering the mix for the first time in 2026); MediaTek jumps 1.5% → 7.3% on the Google TPU program. Useful as an independent supply-side cross-check on the Trainium unit marks already carried (UBS · Sunny Lin: 1.8mn units '26E / 2.8mn '27E) — the wafer trajectory is directionally consistent with that ramp.

events.src: Goldman Sachs · Eric Sheridan / Gabriela Borges / Jim Schneider
events.text: 'Sizing the AI Economy Needed to Justify ROIC on Hyperscaler AI Capex' — six US hyperscalers need ~$1.42trn of CY2028-30 revenue (~$11.6bn/GW/yr) for a 15% ROIC on ~$1.73trn of Phase-2 (CY26-27) AI capex at ~$42bn/GW, 70/30 compute/shells. AMZN (GSe AWS-segment capex): $424.3bn → 10GW → $347.8bn of CY28-30 revenue required = 67.7% of the $513.9bn C2Q26 backlog (MSFT 39.6%, GOOGL 77.7%). Amazon's ~3-yr server breakeven / 30+-yr shell framing is the cohort reference case. Buy, PT $375 (SOTP; $375 since 31-Jul-26, from $335 — page had been stale).

events.src: Goldman Sachs Portfolio Strategy · Ryan Hammond / Ben Snider
events.text: 'AI capex, required revenues, and what's priced in the AI trade' — hyperscaler capex $800bn in 2026, consensus $1.1trn in 2027 (GSe $1.2trn '27 / $1.4trn '28; growth ~100% → 54% → 12%); ~$300bn/yr of AI revenue needed to break even. AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT/ORCL cloud growth 25% (2024) → 48% (Q2 2026), ~$70bn annualised above the 2024 trend; AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT backlog ~$1.7trn. Hyperscalers at their lowest P/E in over a decade. Strategy note, no AMZN rating.

'AI Summit Recap: Still Early with Demand Outstripping Supply' — AMZN a top pick with MSFT and GOOGL. Expert Bill MacCartney views AMZN as a beneficiary of AI infra demand and model hosting but not a likely winner at the frontier-model layer. Exa spends $100M/yr on compute, largely on AWS, and calls AWS inference chips 'good enough'.

events.src: Morgan Stanley · Simeon Gutman / Brian Nowak et al.
events.text: 'Muse: Rewriting the Retail/Consumer Playbook' — AMZN and EBAY screen among the best positioned in e-commerce; META/AMZN/EBAY the Internet clearest winners. 'We think AMZN is well positioned and expect an eventual agreement with Muse.' Handshake Model plus loyalty (data trust, fulfilment trust) keep the transaction with the retailer; retail media is the exposed economics, and Amazon's Muse block 'underscores precisely this tension'. Early agent take rates near zero. AMZN Overweight, no PT stated.

events.src: Jefferies expert call · Horizon Media digital-media executive
events.text: Capstone call notes — agency digital budgets ~+10% y/y (planning ~+10% for 2027); split 30-35% Google / 30-35% Meta / ~30% diversified; 'Amazon's ad offering is also gaining share and scale' on scale, lower-funnel outcomes and first-party data. CTV buying shifting from DSPs (TTD) toward direct deals with Prime Video, Netflix, Disney, Paramount. Retail-media growth slowing as offerings mature.
